```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("../../R/portal_config.R")
cfg <- portal_cfg
rel <- portal_release
v2_current <- rel$is_current(cfg)
```

```{r status}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
if (v2_current) {
  cat(
    "::: {.callout-note appearance=\"simple\"}\n",
    "Release ", cfg$release, " is the current release. It covers the days ",
    rel$coverage_text(cfg), ".\n",
    ":::\n", sep = "")
} else {
  cat(
    "::: {.callout-note appearance=\"simple\"}\n",
    "Release ", cfg$release, " is the upcoming release: its files are being produced, ",
    "starting with the days from ", rel$day_text(cfg$release_coverage$start), ". ",
    "The data available today are those of release ", cfg$current_release,
    ", described on [Release ", cfg$current_release, "](v0.0.2.qmd).\n",
    ":::\n", sep = "")
}
```

This page lists everything a row of the OPDI files can hold: every column of
the flight list and of the flight events, every event type, and the fields of
the `info` column of each event type. It also explains the three version
columns and how the tables join. It describes release v2.0.0 with the default
settings of the OPDI software.

The column tables are written from the software's own list of published
columns, so they always match the files.

## How to read the tables

- **Type** is the type of the stored value: `string` (text), `double` (a
  number with decimals), `boolean` (true or false), `date`, or `timestamp` (a
  date and time).
- **Unit** is the unit of the value. Every time is in UTC (Coordinated
  Universal Time). Altitudes are in feet (ft), distances in nautical miles
  (NM, 1 NM = 1,852 m), durations in seconds (s) or minutes (min), angles in
  degrees.
- An empty value (NULL) means that the item was not detected or is not known.
  It never stands for zero.

## Flight list {#flight-list}

One row per flight. The file of a day holds the flights first seen on that
day (UTC). A **flight** here is a **track**: the sequence of position reports
of one aircraft that OPDI treats as one flight (see
[Track identity](../methods/track-identity.qmd)).

{{< include _generated/flight_list_columns.md >}}

### How the airports were found {#airport-source}

The columns `adep_source` and `ades_source` say how the departure and the
destination airport were found. They hold one of four values:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `aerodrome` | An airport was named from the trajectory: from the first position for the departure, from the descent near an airport for the destination. |
| `out_of_area` | The track began in the air near the edge of the area covered, so the flight came from outside it (departure only). This value is not used when the area covered is the whole world. |
| `undetermined` | No airport could be named. |
| `runway_event` | The airport was taken from a take-off or landing detected on a runway, replacing the value found from the trajectory. |

[Departure and destination airports](../methods/airports.qmd) explains each
case.

## Flight events {#flight-events}

One row per event. An **event** is a moment in a flight, with a time and a
position. A row of the flight events file has three parts, in this order:

1. the columns of the event, listed in the table below;
2. the [measurement columns](#measurements) of the event;
3. the columns of the event's flight, with the same names and meanings as in
   the [flight list](#flight-list), except two: the flight list's `version` is
   called `flight_version` here (the event has a `version` of its own), and
   `flight_id` appears once, among the event columns.

{{< include _generated/flight_events_columns.md >}}

Every published event has a time. Events that the aircraft's own track
clearly contradicts, such as an in-block time while the aircraft is still
flying, are not published (see
[Plausibility checks](../methods/plausibility-checks.qmd)).

## Measurements {#measurements}

A **measurement** is a number attached to an event. Each measurement is a
column of the flight events file. A measurement that does not apply to an
event is empty on that row (see [Empty measurement columns](#empty-measurements)).

{{< include _generated/measurement_columns.md >}}

How these are computed: [Measurements](../methods/measurements.qmd),
[Holding](../methods/holding.qmd) and [Point merge](../methods/point-merge.qmd).

## Flight index and catalogue {#flight-index-and-catalogue}

### Flight index

One file per month, `index/flight_index_YYYYMM.parquet`, with one row per
flight of the month. It tells which daily file holds a flight.

{{< include _generated/flight_index_columns.md >}}

### Catalogue

One file, `catalogue.parquet`, with one row per published day.

{{< include _generated/catalogue_columns.md >}}

## Event types {#event-types}

The column `type` names what an event is. A name with a part in braces
stands for a family of types: `xing-fl{level}` covers `xing-fl50`,
`xing-fl70`, `xing-fl100` and `xing-fl245`. Each line links to the page that
explains how the event is found and how accurate it is.

### Take-off and landing

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `take-off-roll` | The aircraft starts its take-off run on the runway. [Take-off and landing](../methods/takeoff-landing.qmd) |
| `ATOT` | Actual take-off time: the wheels leave the runway. [Take-off and landing](../methods/takeoff-landing.qmd) |
| `xing-runway-threshold` | The aircraft passes over the runway threshold (the start of the landing part of the runway), a few seconds before touchdown. [Take-off and landing](../methods/takeoff-landing.qmd) |
| `ALDT` | Actual landing time: the wheels touch the runway. [Take-off and landing](../methods/takeoff-landing.qmd) |

### Other runway events

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `line-up` | A departing aircraft enters the runway to take off. [Runway milestones](../methods/runway-milestones.qmd) |
| `runway-vacated` | An arriving aircraft leaves the runway after landing. [Runway milestones](../methods/runway-milestones.qmd) |
| `runway-crossing-entry` | A taxiing aircraft enters a runway in order to cross it. [Runway milestones](../methods/runway-milestones.qmd) |
| `runway-crossing-vacated` | The same aircraft leaves the runway on the other side. [Runway milestones](../methods/runway-milestones.qmd) |
| `go-around` | An approaching aircraft gives up the landing and climbs away; placed at the lowest point of the approach. [Runway milestones](../methods/runway-milestones.qmd) |

### Block times

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `AOBT` | Actual off-block time: the aircraft starts to move away from its parking position (stand). [Block times](../methods/block-times.qmd) |
| `AIBT` | Actual in-block time: the aircraft stops at its stand after landing. [Block times](../methods/block-times.qmd) |

### Airport surface

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `entry-{element}` | The aircraft enters an area of the airport. `{element}` is `taxiway`, `apron`, `parking_position` (a stand), `threshold`, `hangar` or `deicing_pad`, for example `entry-taxiway`. [Airport surface events](../methods/surface-events.qmd) |
| `exit-{element}` | The aircraft leaves that area, for example `exit-parking_position`. [Airport surface events](../methods/surface-events.qmd) |

### Vertical profile

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `top-of-climb` | End of the climb to cruise, with the method of EUROCONTROL's vertical flight efficiency indicators. [Vertical events](../methods/vertical-events.qmd) |
| `top-of-descent` | Start of the final descent, with the same method. [Vertical events](../methods/vertical-events.qmd) |
| `level-start` | Start of a period of level flight, cruise included. [Vertical events](../methods/vertical-events.qmd) |
| `level-end` | End of that period. [Vertical events](../methods/vertical-events.qmd) |
| `level-off-climb-start` | Start of a level-off during the climb: level flight below the cruise. [Vertical events](../methods/vertical-events.qmd) |
| `level-off-climb-end` | End of that level-off. [Vertical events](../methods/vertical-events.qmd) |
| `level-off-descent-start` | Start of a level-off during the descent. [Vertical events](../methods/vertical-events.qmd) |
| `level-off-descent-end` | End of that level-off. [Vertical events](../methods/vertical-events.qmd) |
| `xing-fl{level}` | A crossing of flight level 50, 70, 100 or 245 (`xing-fl50`, `xing-fl70`, `xing-fl100`, `xing-fl245`), up or down. [Vertical events](../methods/vertical-events.qmd) |

A **flight level** is an altitude in hundreds of feet on the standard air
pressure of 1013.25 hPa: flight level 100 is about 10,000 ft.

### Distance rings

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `xing-{radius}nm` | A crossing of a circle of 40, 50, 60, 100, 110 or 120 NM around the flight's departure or destination airport (`xing-40nm` to `xing-120nm`). [Distance rings](../methods/distance-rings.qmd) |

### Holding

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `holding-start` | First turning sample of a holding pattern: a loop flown while waiting for permission to continue. [Holding](../methods/holding.qmd) |
| `holding-end` | Last turning sample of the holding pattern. Carries the holding measurements. [Holding](../methods/holding.qmd) |

### Point merge

A **point merge system** is an arrival procedure in which aircraft fly along
an arc, called a leg, at a fixed distance from a merge point until they are
sent directly to it.

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pms-leg-entry` | The aircraft starts flying along a leg. [Point merge](../methods/point-merge.qmd) |
| `pms-leg-exit` | The aircraft leaves the leg towards the merge point. Carries the point merge measurements. [Point merge](../methods/point-merge.qmd) |
| `pms-merge-point` | The aircraft passes closest to a merge point, within 3 NM of it. [Point merge](../methods/point-merge.qmd) |

### Airspace

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `xing-fir` | The flight passes from one flight information region (FIR) or upper information region (UIR) to another. [FIR crossings](../methods/fir-crossings.qmd) |

### Track limits

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `first_seen` | The first position report of the track. [First seen and last seen](../methods/first-last-seen.qmd) |
| `last_seen` | The last position report of the track. [First seen and last seen](../methods/first-last-seen.qmd) |

Event types of release v0.0.2 that release v2.0.0 no longer publishes, such
as `take-off`, `first-xing-fl{level}` and `entry-runway`, are listed with
their replacements on [Releases](releases.qmd#moving-from-v0.0.2).

## Fields of the info column {#info-fields}

The column `info` holds extra details about an event as JSON text, for
example `{"apt_icao": "EGLL", "runway": "27R", ...}`. The fields depend on the
event type. A field without a value is left out of the text. An empty `info`
(an empty text) means that the event type has no extra details.

### Take-off, landing and other runway events

`take-off-roll`, `ATOT`, `xing-runway-threshold`, `ALDT`, `line-up`, `runway-vacated`,
`runway-crossing-entry`, `runway-crossing-vacated`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `apt_icao` | ICAO code of the airport. |
| `runway` | Runway direction used, for example `27R`. |
| `rwy_ident` | The same runway direction, under the name used by earlier releases. |
| `runway_bearing_deg` | True bearing of the runway centre line, in degrees clockwise from true north. |
| `traversal_class` | Class of the runway pass the event comes from: `departure`, `arrival` or `crossing`. |
| `align_deg` | Angle between the aircraft's track and the runway, in degrees. |
| `max_gs_kt` | Highest ground speed during the runway pass, in knots (kt). |
| `osn_flight_id` | Call sign received during the runway pass. |
| `milestone` | Standard number of the moment in airport collaborative decision making (A-CDM): `T06` line-up, `T07` take-off roll, `T08` take-off, `T16` threshold, `T17` touchdown, `T19` runway vacated. Not set on runway crossings. |
| `method` | On `ATOT` and `ALDT` only: `acdm` when the time was found on the runway, as above. |

An `ATOT` or `ALDT` that could not be found on the runway is found from the
climb or the descent instead (see [Take-off and landing](../methods/takeoff-landing.qmd#how-it-is-computed)).
Its `info` holds other fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `method` | `legacy`. |
| `apt_icao` | ICAO code of the airport. |
| `runway` | Runway direction used. |
| `runway_bearing_deg` | True bearing of the runway centre line, in degrees. |
| `role` | `departure` or `arrival`. |
| `bearing_error_deg` | Angle between the aircraft's median track and the runway, in degrees. |
| `n_samples` | Number of position reports the time was found from. |

### Go-around

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `apt_icao` | ICAO code of the destination airport. |
| `osn_flight_id` | Call sign received. |
| `low_height_ft` | Lowest height above the airport during the approach, in feet. |
| `recovery_roc_ft_min` | Highest rate of climb after that point, in feet per minute. |
| `excursion_seconds` | Duration of the excursion, in seconds. |

### Block times

| Event type | Field | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `AOBT` | `stand_exit` | Time of the stand exit that belongs to this off-block: the first exit from a stand area at or after it in the same part of the track, otherwise the last one before it. Absent when that part holds no stand exit. |
| `AOBT` | `stand` | Name in OpenStreetMap of the stand of `stand_exit`, when it has one. |
| `AOBT` | `apt_icao` | ICAO code of the airport of that stand. |
| `AIBT` | `stand_entry` | Time of the stand entry that belongs to this in-block: the last entry into a stand area at or before it in the same part of the track, otherwise the first one after it. Absent when that part holds no stand entry. |
| `AIBT` | `stand` | Name in OpenStreetMap of the stand of `stand_entry`, when it has one. |
| `AIBT` | `apt_icao` | ICAO code of the airport of that stand. |

### Airport surface

`entry-{element}` and `exit-{element}`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `osm_id` | Identifier of the area in OpenStreetMap, the open map of the world. |
| `osm_aeroway` | Kind of area, as named in OpenStreetMap, for example `taxiway`. |
| `osm_ref` | Name or number of the area in OpenStreetMap, for example a stand number. |
| `osm_airport` | ICAO code of the airport. |
| `opdi_time_in_use_s` | Time spent in the area, in seconds. |
| `osn_icao24` | ICAO 24-bit address of the aircraft. |
| `osn_flight_id` | Call sign received. |

### Top of climb and top of descent

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `d200_time` | Time of the top as first found, before it was moved. |
| `d200_altitude_ft` | Altitude of the top as first found, in feet. |
| `relocated` | `true` when the top was moved, `false` otherwise. |
| `analysis_radius_nm` | Radius of the analysis around the airport, in NM (200). |
| `method` | `pru`: the method of the EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit. |

### Level-offs

`level-off-climb-start`, `level-off-climb-end`, `level-off-descent-start`,
`level-off-descent-end`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `kpi` | ICAO indicator the level-off counts for: `KPI17` (climb) or `KPI19` (descent). |
| `duration_s` | Duration of the level-off, in seconds. |
| `distance_nm` | Distance flown during the level-off, in NM. |
| `level_ft` | Altitude of the level-off, in feet. |

### Flight-level crossings

`xing-fl{level}`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `crossing_seq` | Number of the crossing of that level on the flight, 1 for the first. |
| `direction` | `up` or `down`. |
| `bracket_s` | Time between the two position reports the crossing was placed between, in seconds. |

### Distance rings

`xing-{radius}nm`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `apt_icao` | ICAO code of the airport the circle is drawn around. |
| `direction` | `inbound` (towards the airport) or `outbound`. |
| `crossing_seq` | Number of the crossing of this circle on the flight, 1 for the first. |
| `bearing` | Direction of the crossing point seen from the airport, in degrees clockwise from true north. |
| `flight_level` | Flight level of the aircraft at the crossing. |
| `bracket_s` | Time between the two position reports the crossing was placed between, in seconds. |

### Holding

`holding-start` and `holding-end` carry the same fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `holding_seq` | Number of the holding pattern on the flight, 1 for the first. |
| `pattern` | `racetrack` or `orbit`. |
| `direction` | Direction of turn: `R` (right) or `L` (left). |
| `circuits` | Number of loops: total turn divided by 360 degrees, to one decimal. |
| `duration_s` | Time in the holding pattern, in seconds. |
| `distance_nm` | Distance flown in it, in NM. |
| `altitude_start_ft` | Altitude at the start, in feet. |
| `altitude_end_ft` | Altitude at the end, in feet. |
| `straight_pct` | Share of the time flown straight, in percent. |

### Point merge

`pms-leg-entry` and `pms-leg-exit` carry the same fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `apt_icao` | ICAO code of the airport the system serves. |
| `pms_id` | Identifier of the point merge system. |
| `merge_point` | Name of the merge point. |
| `leg_seq` | Number of the leg flown on the flight, 1 for the first. |
| `direction` | Direction of flight along the arc: `cw` (clockwise) or `ccw` (counter-clockwise). |
| `leg_distance_nm` | Distance of the leg from the merge point, in NM. |
| `leg_level_ft` | Altitude on the leg, in feet. |
| `duration_s` | Time on the leg, in seconds. |
| `distance_nm` | Distance flown along the leg, in NM. |
| `direct_to_distance_nm` | Distance to the merge point when the aircraft left the leg, in NM. |
| `direct_aligned` | `true` when the aircraft then flew a straight line to the merge point. |

`pms-merge-point`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `apt_icao` | ICAO code of the airport the system serves. |
| `pms_id` | Identifier of the point merge system. |
| `merge_point` | Name of the merge point. |
| `closest_nm` | Closest distance to the merge point, in NM. |
| `via_leg` | `true` when the aircraft flew a leg of the system just before. |

### FIR crossings

`xing-fir`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `crossing_seq` | Number of the crossing on the flight, 1 for the first. |
| `fir_from` | The region left, for example `EGTTFIR`. |
| `fir_to` | The region entered. |
| `fl` | Flight level at the crossing. |
| `bracket_s` | Time between the last position report in the old region and the first in the new one, in seconds. |
| `airac_cfmu` | The AIRAC cycle of the boundaries used (524). An AIRAC cycle is the 28-day period in which aeronautical data such as airspace boundaries take effect. |
| `airac_validity_start` | First day of that cycle. |
| `airac_validity_end` | Last day of that cycle. |

### Events without details

`level-start`, `level-end`, `first_seen` and `last_seen` have an empty `info`.

## Source {#source}

The column `source` names where the position reports of an event come from.
In release v2.0.0 it is always `OSN`, for the OpenSky Network.

## Versions and release {#versions}

Three columns say which method and which release produced a row. They
answer different questions.

| Column | Where | What it names | Values in release v2.0.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `release` | every row of both files | The data release the row belongs to. It is the same on every row of a release. | `v2.0.0` |
| `version` | flight list | The method that built the flight list row. | `v5.0.0` |
| `flight_version` | flight events | The same value as `version` of the event's flight in the flight list. | `v5.0.0` |
| `version` | flight events | The method that produced the event. Different event types can have different versions. A method that changes gets a new version, so older data stay reproducible. | see below |

The event versions of release v2.0.0:

| Version | Event types |
|---|---|
| `events_v0.3.0` | runway events, block times, airport surface, vertical profile, distance rings, `first_seen`, `last_seen` |
| `holding_v0.1.0` | `holding-start`, `holding-end` |
| `pms_v0.1.0` | `pms-leg-entry`, `pms-leg-exit`, `pms-merge-point` |
| `fir_v0.1.0` | `xing-fir` |

The measurement columns have no version column of their own. Their versions
are:

| Measurement columns | Version |
|---|---|
| `distance_flown_nm` | `distance_v0.0.3` |
| `time_passed_s` | `time_v0.0.1` |
| `holding_duration_s`, `holding_distance_nm`, `holding_circuits` | `holding_v0.1.0` |
| `pms_leg_time_s`, `pms_leg_distance_nm`, `pms_direct_to_distance_nm` | `pms_v0.1.0` |

The `measurements` view (see [Access](access.qmd#tables-and-views)) gives each
measured value as a row with this version in its `version` column.

## Identifiers and joins {#identifiers}

| Identifier | Names | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `flight_id` | a flight (track) | The first 16 characters of the SHA-256 hash of the aircraft address, an underscore, and the time of the track's first position in seconds since 1970-01-01 (Unix time), for example `3f9a0c1d2b4e5f60_1781412334`. |
| `event_id` | an event | 32 hexadecimal characters, computed from the flight, the event type, the time and the version of the event. The same event gets the same identifier when a day is processed again. |
| `icao24` | an aircraft's transponder | Six hexadecimal characters, for example `4ca123`. |
| `flt_id` | the call sign | As broadcast, for example `DLH123`. |

How the tables join:

- **Flight events to flight list**: on `flight_id`. Most of the time this join
  is not needed, because every event row already carries the columns of its
  flight.
- **Flight index to flight list**: on `flight_id`; the column `file` names the
  daily flight list file that holds the flight.
- **The views of the release v0.0.2 shape**: `events.id` is the `event_id`,
  `measurements.event_id` joins to `events.id`, and `events.flight_id` joins to
  `flight_list_v0.id` (the view and the Python reader both write the
  column as `id`, in lower case).
- **To the OpenSky Network's own data**: with `icao24`, the call sign and the
  time span from `first_seen` to `last_seen`, the position reports of a flight
  can be fetched from the OpenSky Network's historical database, for example
  with the tools listed on its [data tools page](https://opensky-network.org/data/data-tools).

A `flight_id` depends on the method that built the track. Identifiers of
different releases do not match, so data of release v0.0.2 and of release
v2.0.0 cannot be joined on `flight_id`. Join on `icao24`, call sign and time
instead.

## Empty measurement columns {#empty-measurements}

Most events have a `distance_flown_nm` and a `time_passed_s`. The other
measurement columns belong to one event type each.

| Measurement columns | Set on | Empty on |
|---|---|---|
| `distance_flown_nm`, `time_passed_s` | nearly every event | `AOBT`, `AIBT`, the four level-off types, and `ATOT` and `ALDT` found from the climb or the descent (`method` = `legacy` in `info`) |
| `holding_duration_s`, `holding_distance_nm`, `holding_circuits` | `holding-end` | every other event type, `holding-start` included |
| `pms_leg_time_s`, `pms_leg_distance_nm`, `pms_direct_to_distance_nm` | `pms-leg-exit` | every other event type, `pms-leg-entry` included |

Why some events have no distance or time is explained in
[Measurements](../methods/measurements.qmd#limitations).
